cicd.strategy: GitHub Actions mono-pipeline. Single workflow file with conditional stages triggered by push/PR/schedule. GitHub Actions is free for public repos, already integrated with GitHub, and Railway has native GitHub integration that auto-deploys on push to main.
stages: deploy (Railway auto-deploy on push to main)
cicd.rollback_procedure: Railway supports instant rollback to any previous deployment via dashboard or CLI. SQLite lives on a Railway volume so rollback only affects app code. For data rollback: delete jobs where fetched_at > rollback timestamp using runs table as audit trail.

observability.logging: Replace all print() with Python stdlib logging. Structured JSON logging via logging.config.dictConfig() in job_monitor/logging_config.py. Module-level loggers: logger = logging.getLogger(__name__). JSON lines in production (python-json-logger), human-readable locally.

slos.name: freshness
slos.target: New jobs appear within 2 hours of posting

slos.name: scraper_success_rate
slos.target: At least 3 of 5 scrapers succeed per run

slos.name: data_quality
slos.target: Less than 5% filtered jobs have empty descriptions

alerting: All scrapers failed in a single run
Scraper success rate below 60% for 3 consecutive runs
dashboards: Pipeline Health tab in Streamlit: jobs per source, new jobs trend, scraper success rates, score distribution over time, last successful run per source

pyramid.unit: 40-50 tests: filters.py (matches_title, title_not_excluded, matches_keywords, is_geo_excluded), scorer.py (all _score_* functions, _parse_salary, _detect_currency), dedup._url_hash, models.Job validation
pyramid.integration: 15-20 tests: DB operations (init_db, save_jobs, load_jobs, dedup), full filter pipeline, full scoring pipeline with tmp_path SQLite
pyramid.e2e: 8-12 tests: scraper integration with mocked HTTP (responses library), full pipeline dry_run, retry on 429
pyramid.load: Deferred — SQLite handles current scale fine. Add EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN benchmarks if hitting 100k+ jobs.

testing_strategy.ai_evaluation: Not applicable — scorer is rule-based and deterministic. Standard unit tests with exact assertions. Would switch to eval sets if adding LLM scoring layer.

deployment.model: Single-service on Railway. Two processes: (1) Streamlit dashboard (always-on), (2) Scraper runner (GitHub Actions cron every 6h).
deployment.iac_tool: Dockerfile (multi-stage, Python 3.12-slim) + railway.toml. No Terraform needed at this scale.
deployment.release_strategy: Trunk-based development. Push to main = deploy. Feature branches + PRs for non-trivial changes. CI pipeline is the staging gate.
deployment.secrets_management: Railway env vars for production. GitHub Actions secrets for CI. Local .env in .gitignore. No secrets vault needed — all scrapers use public APIs.
deployment.environment_parity: Dockerfile ensures identical Python + deps between CI and prod. python-version: 3.12 in GitHub Actions matrix.

data_governance.lineage: Add run_id FK to jobs table so every job traces to its pipeline run. Already have source field and runs table.
data_governance.schema_versioning: schema_version table + sequential migration SQL files in migrations/ folder. Formalize existing ad-hoc ALTER TABLE pattern.
data_governance.pii_handling: No PII collected. All data is public job postings. No GDPR/LGPD concerns.
data_governance.model_versioning: Add SCORER_VERSION constant in scorer.py, store in score_breakdown JSON. Enables re-scoring when weights change.
data_governance.output_auditing: Add total_scored, avg_score, duration_seconds columns to runs table.

scanning: GitHub secret scanning (free for public repos)
security.iam_approach: No auth on dashboard — acceptable for read-only public job data. Add Streamlit password protection if needed later.
owasp_mitigations: SQL injection: already mitigated — parameterized queries throughout
XSS: add html.escape() on rendered fields in dashboard (defense-in-depth over _strip_html)
SSRF: low risk — outbound requests to hardcoded domains only
Dependency confusion: pin exact versions with pip-compile

cost_controls.budget_alerts: Railway free tier $5/month — set spending limit. GitHub Actions free for public repos (2000 min/month, pipeline uses ~5 min/run).
cost_controls.caching_strategy: requests-cache for dev (avoid hitting APIs during testing). Production uses fresh data. st.cache_data(ttl=300) already handles dashboard caching.
cost_controls.model_tier_policy: No AI/LLM models — scorer is pure Python. If adding LLM summarization later, use Haiku (cheapest). Rule-based scorer costs $0/month vs ~$150/month for LLM at scale.
